subject: PHI surface & eligible deployment modes — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: PHI surface & eligible deployment modes — follow-up and next steps

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the call earlier — useful to understand Medicore's use case. Quick recap on the HIPAA-specific items we discussed and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) PHI surface: from our discussion, you expect the LLM invocation to receive diagnostic summaries and patient identifiers in ~15% of requests (primarily study ingestion). We flagged two buckets: direct PHI (names, MRNs) and de-identified clinical text. Please confirm if any attachments (DICOM metadata, PDFs) will be passed to the API in production.

2) Eligible deployment modes: based on the PHI risk, we outlined three options — Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem), Dedicated reserved capacity with strict tenancy separation, or Hosted with a BAA and strict redaction rules. For PHI with full identifiers we recommended Redwood Private / on-prem.

3) BAA availability & timeline: we can provide a standard BAA and a draft copy (attached) within 24-48 hours for initial review. Legal review and signature typically follow via DocuSign.

4) Evidence & questionnaire: your security team asked for SOC 2 attestation and a starting vendor security questionnaire. I attached a short HIPAA summary sheet and our suggested evidence list. For SOC 2 we are currently Type II; I can loop in our compliance owner for an evidence package.

Next steps I propose (action owners in parentheses):
- Confirm whether attachments/DICOM metadata will be passed to the service (Medicore: Lena)
- Confirm preferred deployment mode if PHI will be present (Medicore: Procurement + Security)
- I will share the BAA draft and vendor questionnaire and ask compliance for SOC 2 artifacts (Rishi)
- If Private deployment looks required, schedule a quick technical call with our infra SE (Priyom) to scope networking and HSM/KMS needs (Medicore + Priyom)

I've attached the BAA draft and PHI summary for your legal/security team to scan. Happy to sync again this week.

Best,

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments:
- redwood_baa_draft_v1.pdf (stub)
- hipaa_summary_sheet.xlsx (stub)

From: Dr. Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>

Cc: Julian Smith <julian.smith@medicore.com>, Procurement <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI surface & eligible deployment modes — follow-up and next steps

Hi Rishi,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We will NOT send raw DICOM files for initial beta. We may send extracted metadata fields (study ID, modality) and clinical notes that include names/IDs in ~10–15% of records.
- Our security team prefers Private or Dedicated for any workload that includes direct identifiers. Hosted + BAA is acceptable only if we implement upstream de-identification (which adds latency and engineering effort).
- Procurement: target timeline for contract execution is end of Q3; security wants the vendor questionnaire and SOC 2 artifacts for their risk review by 6/18.

Can you get the SOC 2 Type II report and the vendor questionnaire to Julian? I've cc'd him. Also please confirm whether Redwood supports HSM-backed KMS in Private deployments.

Thanks,

Lena Ortiz, MD
VP Clinical Informatics | Medicore Health
lena.ortiz@medicore.com

Julian / Procurement team,

Thanks for the quick reply, Lena — looping in our compliance and infra leads so we can get your security team everything they need by 6/18. Summary of what I'm attaching and the immediate asks: 

Attachments (stubs):
- vendor-soc2-evidence-ask.docx (checklist of what Medicore typically requests and what we can produce)
- redwood_baa_draft_v1.pdf (initial BAA for review)

Immediate answers: 
- SOC 2 status: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (policy and evidence available). I will gather the standard report and a short evidence bundle (to be shared via our secure drive link).
- HSM-backed KMS: yes — Private deployments can integrate with customer-managed HSMs or cloud KMS; we will coordinate details on key rotation policies and network placement.

Action items: 
- Julian: can you confirm the preferred method to transfer evidence (secure link or SFTP)?
- Procurement: confirm whether Medicore wants a Dedicated reserved cluster or a Private VPC deployment in the initial PoC if we include direct identifiers. If you prefer Dedicated, we can scope tenancy and encryption requirements.
- Priyom / Marissa (internal): Priyom — can you prepare an infra checklist for Private + Dedicated options (networking, KMS, audit logs), and Marissa please flag any commercial constraints we should expect for an enterprise BAA + Dedicated commit.

I'll target getting the SOC 2/package link and BAA DocuSign by end of day tomorrow.

Regards,

Rishi,

Thanks for the attachments. Procurement prefers Private VPC for the PoC given the identifiers; that said, Dedicated could be shelfed for later if cost/ops tradeoffs favor it. For evidence transfer please provide a secure, expiring download link to the SOC 2 Type II report and the artifact bundle. SFTP is not preferred.

Also: a couple quick questions for your checklist (Priyom):
- Can audit logs show token-level request traces for at least 180 days?
- Do you support per-customer key rotation schedules and customer-provided KMS keys?

If you can confirm these by EOD we can put the vendor questionnaire into our review queue. Once we get a packaging of evidence we will share a redline timeline.
